also: how much do I owe you?

evidence: Vulg. Lc. 16.5: quantum dēbēs dominō meō?
terms.comment: What is owed in the accusative, the creditor in the dative: pecūniam alicui dēbēre; a debt is dēbitum or aes aliēnum (see debt). With an infinitive dēbeō is ought, of duty (see be supposed to).

phrases.latin: Sexte, nihil dēbēs, nīl dēbēs, Sexte, fatēmur: dēbet enim, sī quis solvere, Sexte, potest.
phrases.english: You owe nothing, Sextus, nothing at all, Sextus, we admit it: for only a man who can pay owes anything, Sextus.

phrases.latin: quantum dēbēs dominō meō? at ille dīxit: centum cadōs oleī.
phrases.english: How much do you owe my master? And he said: A hundred jars of oil.

phrases.latin: Aesōpī nōmen sīcubi interposuerō, cui reddidī jam prīdem quicquid dēbuī, auctōritātis esse scītō grātiā
phrases.english: If I bring in Aesop’s name anywhere, though I paid him long ago all I owed him, know that it is for the sake of his authority

sources: Lewis & Short: debeo
